deviations: One fix commit (9b9fb90) carries both decided changes: the line test at the token start, and the run of signs in NumberEnd and NumberRunsInto. Their source texts are interleaved (the same remarks speak of both), so split commits would each have needed a second, interim wording. Footer: Refs #156, #188, #281.

NumberRunsInto: `streamStart >= spanStart` is hoisted to guard both arms and replaces `streamStart >= 0`. This is equivalent on the first arm: a candidate inside the window can never precede a streamStart that lies before it. The sign arm has no `candidate > streamStart` condition, because a candidate at streamStart maps to itself. Both choices avoid leaving equivalent mutants.

NumberEnd skips the sign run past the first byte unconditionally (the first prototype's form) and has no Math.Max. A digit-first header holds only digits up to the white space after them. Every place passed lies whole in the bytes searched, with 'obj' (or the rest of 'xref') past it. The remark says this.

HeaderTokenStart (private, span indices) walks back while first > 0, then requires first >= from and a '+' at first. This follows the triage's guards literally: the window's and the file's first byte, and a run within the bytes searched. It needs a file-start row and two window-edge rows to kill its bound mutants, all added.
